fah-266.title: Shorik Bread
fah-266.culturalNotes: A regular oven works if you don't have a griddle — it just needs very high heat.

instructions.1: Mix a cup of warm milk and a cup of warm water with a teaspoon of sugar, a teaspoon of yeast and a pinch of salt.
instructions.2: Stir well until the sugar, salt and yeast dissolve.
instructions.3: Cover and leave for 10 minutes until the yeast starts reacting.
instructions.4: Add two tablespoons of oil and mix.
instructions.5: Add 6 cups of flour and mix until the dough comes together.
instructions.6: Coat the dough with two tablespoons of oil and prove in a warm place for half an hour.
instructions.7: Cut the dough into 4 equal pieces and shape each into a ball.
instructions.8: Cover the balls with a clean cloth and leave for 10 minutes.
instructions.9: Roll each ball on a lightly floured surface.
instructions.10: Put the rolled dough on an oiled griddle and brush the top with egg beaten with a teaspoon of vanilla.
instructions.11: Sprinkle with sesame and nigella seeds.
instructions.12: Bake in a very hot oven until browned on all sides.
instructions.13: Serve the shorik hot with charred cauliflower, watercress, olives and black honey.

fah-267.title: Sameed & Duqqa (Damietta Sesame Bread)
fah-267.culturalNotes: The dough should be smooth and cohesive before proving. Add black pepper to the duqqa if you like. Sameed keeps in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the flours in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the milk powder, sugar, yeast, salt and sesame. Mix well.
instructions.3: Add the oil and warm water. Knead until the dough is smooth and cohesive.
instructions.4: Cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes until doubled.
instructions.5: Cut the dough into small lemon-sized balls.
instructions.6: Cover the balls and leave for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Thin the date molasses with water and mix well.
instructions.8: Grind the duqqa (peanuts, sesame, almonds, cumin, coriander, salt) coarsely in the grinder.
instructions.9: Shape each ball into a coil, dip it in the date-molasses mix, then in the sesame.
instructions.10: Lay the sameed on an oiled tray and prove for 30 minutes.
instructions.11: Bake in a preheated 220°C oven for 15–20 minutes until golden.
instructions.12: Serve the sameed hot with the duqqa and a cup of milky tea.

fah-268.title: Mokashkasha (Scrunched Filo Dessert)
fah-268.culturalNotes: Serve mokashkasha hot or cold. It keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Brush two filo sheets with ghee as shown.
instructions.2: Scrunch the sheets together.
instructions.3: Put the scrunched sheets in a ghee-greased tray.
instructions.4: Repeat until all the sheets are used.
instructions.5: Cut the scrunched pastry into small pieces.
instructions.6: Mix the milk and cream caramel together and pour over the pastry.
instructions.7: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 15 minutes.
instructions.8: Take it out when golden.
instructions.9: Pour the syrup over the pastry once it is out of the oven.

fah-269.title: Custard-Filled Brioche
fah-269.culturalNotes: The milk in the dough should be warm, not too hot, or it kills the yeast. Add the raisins to the custard while cooking or scatter them over the brioche after baking.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the 3 egg whites and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the warm milk gradually and knead the dough.
instructions.4: Add the butter and knead for 10 minutes until the dough is soft.
instructions.5: Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover and leave to prove.
instructions.6: In another pot, put 3 cups of milk and half a cup of cream over the heat.
instructions.7: Whisk the 3 egg yolks, a spoon of vanilla, a cup of sugar and 3 tablespoons of cornflour together.
instructions.8: Add the cornflour mix gradually to the hot milk, whisking quickly until the custard is creamy.
instructions.9: Add a spoon of butter to the custard and leave to cool.
instructions.10: Cut the dough into equal balls and rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.11: Roll each ball and cut with a round cutter.
instructions.12: Put the custard filling in the centre of a circle with a few raisins.
instructions.13: Cover the filling with another circle and arrange the brioche on an oiled tray.
instructions.14: Brush the brioche with the egg-and-vanilla mix.
instructions.15: Bake in a hot oven for 10 minutes until golden.

fah-270.title: Homemade Breadsticks (Bo'somat)
fah-270.culturalNotes: Test the yeast before using. Serve the breadsticks with cheese and milky vanilla tea.

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and yeast.
instructions.2: Add half a cup of oil gradually while mixing.
instructions.3: Add the warm water gradually until the dough comes together.
instructions.4: Knead for at least 10 minutes until soft and elastic.
instructions.5: Cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove in a warm place for an hour.
instructions.6: Cut the dough into small, equal pieces.
instructions.7: Roll each piece into a rectangle, twist it and seal the ends well.
instructions.8: Put the breadsticks on an oiled tray, cover and prove for 15 minutes.
instructions.9: In a small bowl, mix the water and sugar and put it in a spray bottle.
instructions.10: Spray the breadsticks with the sugar water and sprinkle sesame and nigella seeds.
instructions.11: Heat the oven to 160°C.
instructions.12: Bake on the middle shelf for 20–25 minutes until golden.
instructions.13: Take the breadsticks out and cool slightly before serving.

fah-271.title: Bakery-Style Bourek
fah-271.culturalNotes: Add pastrami or thyme fillings as you like. Bourek keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Great with tea or coffee.

instructions.1: Mix the dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, yeast, sugar, salt) in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the yogurt and milk powder and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the warm water gradually until the dough is cohesive.
instructions.4: Add the oil and knead for 10 minutes until soft and not sticky.
instructions.5: Add a tablespoon of tomato sauce for a golden colour.
instructions.6: Cover the dough and prove for 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Divide the dough into 4 parts and roll into balls.
instructions.8: Roll each ball under half a centimetre thick.
instructions.9: Cut the dough into circles with a glass or round cutter.
instructions.10: Fill each circle with cheese and your favourite additions (pastrami, thyme, parsley, olives).
instructions.11: Seal the circles tightly like qatayef.
instructions.12: Put the bourek on an oiled tray, spaced apart.
instructions.14: Brush the tops with the glaze mix (milk powder, sugar, coffee, water, egg).
instructions.15: Sprinkle sesame and nigella seeds on top.
instructions.16: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 15–20 minutes until golden.

fah-272.title: Spinach Bourek
fah-272.culturalNotes: The filling freezes well for later pastries. Swap it for cheese and pastrami, minced meat or peppered sausage.

instructions.1: Melt a spoon of butter in a pan over the heat.
instructions.2: Add the chicken cut into small cubes and stir until browned.
instructions.3: Add the minced onion and stir until softened.
instructions.4: Add the salt and pepper and stir well.
instructions.5: Add the washed, chopped spinach and stir until wilted and the liquid dries.
instructions.6: Take the filling off the heat and cool slightly.
instructions.7: Add the cream cheese and mixed cheese (mozzarella and cheddar) and stir well.
instructions.8: In another bowl, mix half a cup of melted butter, a cup of yogurt and a teaspoon of baking powder until combined.
instructions.9: Take a filo sheet and brush with the mix, add another sheet and brush again — repeat to 3–4 layers.
instructions.10: Put the filling in the centre of the sheets and roll carefully.
instructions.11: Repeat until all the sheets are used.
instructions.12: Put the bourek on an oiled tray.
instructions.13: Brush the bourek with two tablespoons of butter.
instructions.14: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 20 minutes until golden.
instructions.15: Cut the bourek and serve hot.

fah-273.title: Eastern Pizza (Feteer Pockets)
fah-273.culturalNotes: Use whatever fillings you have — cheese, cold cuts, chicken. Make sure the fillings are cooked before stuffing the pastry.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the water gradually and knead to a medium-soft dough.
instructions.3: Knead for at least 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Cover and rest for half an hour.
instructions.5: Cut the dough into small balls.
instructions.6: Grease the worktop with butter and oil.
instructions.7: Stretch the dough by hand until very thin.
instructions.8: Make cuts with a knife 10 cm apart.
instructions.9: Put the filling in the centre.
instructions.10: Fold the pastry closed from the sides and brush it.
instructions.11: Lay the pastries on an oiled tray.
instructions.12: Bake at very high heat for 10–15 minutes.
instructions.13: Alternatively, cook them in a pan over medium heat until done on both sides.

fah-274.title: Pastry Assortment with Mixed Fillings
fah-274.culturalNotes: The pastries freeze well wrapped tightly — thaw at room temperature or reheat in the microwave.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and milk powder in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the yogurt and egg white and knead with warm water a little at a time until the dough comes together.
instructions.3: Knead for 10 minutes, adding the butter or oil halfway through.
instructions.4: Cover and prove in a warm place for 30–60 minutes.
instructions.5: In another pan, fry the onion in oil until golden.
instructions.6: Add the mashed potatoes, spices, parsley and mozzarella and stir well.
instructions.7: Prepare the other fillings: cheese mix with cream cheese, thyme and olives; Istanbuli cheese with green pepper; seasoned meat with parsley.
instructions.8: Cut the dough into equal balls and cover.
instructions.9: Roll each ball, fill with the different fillings and shape as you like (croissants, manaqeesh, turnovers).
instructions.10: Brush the pastries with the egg-yolk-and-milk mix.
instructions.11: Lay them on an oiled tray and prove for 10 minutes.
instructions.12: Bake in a hot oven for 15–20 minutes until golden.
instructions.13: Cover the pastries with a clean towel straight out of the oven to keep them soft.

fah-275.title: Party & Birthday Pastry Assortment
fah-275.culturalNotes: Use any cheeses and cold cuts you like. Keep the dough soft and not dry for the best result. The pastries keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast with the warm water and sugar and set aside for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the flour with the salt, baking powder and milk powder.
instructions.3: Add the mayonnaise, yogurt and proved yeast and knead well.
instructions.4: Add the warm water gradually until you get a soft, tacky dough.
instructions.5: Cover the dough and prove for an hour.
instructions.6: Cut the dough into big and small balls.
instructions.7: Shape the small balls into rounds and lay them on an oiled tray.
instructions.8: Shape the big balls into strips and circles.
instructions.9: Add the different fillings — sausages, tuna, cheese, olives, coloured peppers.
instructions.10: Brush the pastries with the milk-powder, sugar and Nescafé glaze.
instructions.11: Sprinkle sesame or nigella seeds.
instructions.12: Bake in a 200°C oven for 20–30 minutes until golden.

fah-276.title: Party Pastry Assortment II
fah-276.culturalNotes: Add fillings like seasoned chicken or minced meat. The pastries keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast with the sugar and warm water and set aside for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the flour with the salt, baking powder and milk powder.
instructions.3: Add the mayonnaise, yogurt and proved yeast and knead well.
instructions.4: Add the warm water gradually until you get a soft, tacky dough.
instructions.5: Cover the dough and prove for an hour.
instructions.6: Cut the dough into big and small balls.
instructions.7: Shape the big balls into forms — mini sandwiches, wrapped sausages, glazed buns and squares.
instructions.8: Fill the pastries with the fillings you like.
instructions.9: Brush with the milk-powder, sugar and Nescafé glaze.
instructions.10: Arrange on an oiled tray and prove for 15 minutes.
instructions.11: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 15–20 minutes until golden.

fah-277.title: Chicken & Cheese Goulash Pie
fah-277.culturalNotes: The chicken filling freezes for later. More milk makes the pastry softer.

instructions.1: Prepare the filo and cut it to the tray's size.
instructions.2: Brush the tray with the butter-and-oil mix.
instructions.3: Layer the filo, brushing each sheet with the butter-oil mix.
instructions.4: Put the cut pieces in the middle to prevent cracking.
instructions.5: Spread the chicken-and-cheese filling in the middle.
instructions.6: Close the tray with the last filo sheet.
instructions.7: Score the top before baking.
instructions.8: Heat the oven to 200°C.
instructions.9: Bake the tray on the middle shelf until nicely coloured.
instructions.10: Mix half a teaspoon of baking powder with half a cup of milk and pour over the tray.
instructions.11: Return to the oven until beautifully browned.
instructions.12: Take out and serve hot.

fah-278.title: Savoury Goulash with Cheese & Fruit
fah-278.culturalNotes: Dust with icing sugar and crushed custard biscuits when serving. Use any cheeses and fruits you like.

instructions.1: Take two filo sheets, cut them to shape and roll them into roses.
instructions.2: Arrange the roses in a ghee-greased tray.
instructions.3: Make the custard mix: blend the custard powder or cornflour with the yogurt, milk, vanilla, melted butter and icing sugar.
instructions.4: Pour the mix over the roses in the tray.
instructions.5: Add a spoon of strawberry jam on each rose.
instructions.6: Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until browned.
instructions.7: Make the yogurt-butter mix: blend the butter, yogurt and baking powder.
instructions.8: Grease an oven tray with oil or ghee and lay filo sheets in it, brushing each layer with the mix.
instructions.9: Put the filling (cheese, peppers, olives, pastrami) in the middle.
instructions.10: Close the tray with the remaining filo and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until browned.
instructions.11: Serve the savoury goulash hot with vanilla ice cream.

fah-279.title: Fajita Filo Roll
fah-279.culturalNotes: Add hot pepper for a spicy kick. The roll keeps in the fridge for two days or longer frozen.

instructions.1: Cut the chicken breasts into small cubes.
instructions.2: Cut the onions, coloured peppers and tomatoes into small cubes.
instructions.3: Mix the chicken with the salt, chicken seasoning, black pepper, onion powder, ketchup and seven-spice.
instructions.4: Leave the mix for an hour to come together.
instructions.5: Heat oil in a pan and stir the chicken until cooked.
instructions.6: Add the onion, peppers and tomatoes and stir for two minutes.
instructions.7: Mix the baking powder with the ghee or butter.
instructions.8: Brush a filo sheet with the mix and lay it on a griddle or tray.
instructions.9: Repeat until you have 6–7 stacked sheets.
instructions.10: Put the filling at one edge of the filo with the cheese mix.
instructions.11: Roll gently and brush the top with the remaining mix.
instructions.12: Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden.
instructions.13: Cut the roll into slices before serving.

fah-280.title: Turkish Balloon Bread
fah-280.culturalNotes: Turkish balloon bread makes sweet or savoury sandwiches. It keeps in a sealed bag for two days.

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix the warm milk with the yeast and sugar. Leave for 10 minutes until the yeast starts reacting.
instructions.2: Add the flour, salt and oil to the yeast mix. Knead until smooth.
instructions.3: Cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes until doubled.
instructions.4: Knock out the air and divide into 6 balls. Cover and prove again for 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Dip each ball in milk, then in white sesame.
instructions.6: Roll each ball on a floured surface to half a centimetre, then cut into 4 parts.
instructions.7: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry each loaf until puffed and golden on both sides.
instructions.8: Drain on paper towels.

fah-281.title: Khobz el-Dar (House Bread)
fah-281.culturalNotes: A toast tin or English cake tin works for a hollow loaf. The bread freezes well for sandwiches.

instructions.1: Mix the flour well in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the warm milk, oil, yeast, salt, egg, egg yolk, sugar and baking powder.
instructions.3: Mix well until combined.
instructions.4: Rest the dough for 10 minutes to prove.
instructions.5: Add the flour gradually until you have a lump-free, pourable batter.
instructions.6: Grease the baking tray with ghee and dust with flour.
instructions.7: Pour the batter in and spread evenly.
instructions.8: Cover and prove for 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Brush the surface with egg white and sprinkle nigella seeds, sesame and flaxseeds.
instructions.10: Put the tray in a preheated 200°C oven.
instructions.11: Bake for 15 minutes until golden.
instructions.12: Take out and cool slightly before serving.

fah-282.title: Breakfast & Supper Bread
fah-282.culturalNotes: Serve with cheese, eggs, honey or anything you like at breakfast or supper. Keeps in a sealed bag for two days.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, milk powder, sugar, yeast and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the egg, vinegar, oil and warm milk gradually and knead until soft and slightly tacky.
instructions.3: Cover and prove in a warm place for an hour until doubled.
instructions.4: Spread the dough on an oiled tray and prove again for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Brush with egg yolk mixed with a little vinegar.
instructions.6: Score the dough into squares and sprinkle sesame and nigella seeds.
instructions.7: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 15–20 minutes until golden.
instructions.8: Cool slightly, then cut and serve.

fah-283.title: Eid Ruqaq (Layered Meat Pastry)
fah-283.culturalNotes: Add nuts, raisins or cheese as you like. The ruqaq keeps in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the flour with the baking powder, sugar and salt.
instructions.2: Add the oil and mix until it looks like wet sand.
instructions.3: Add the warm water gradually until the dough comes together.
instructions.4: Knead well until soft and easy to shape.
instructions.5: Cut the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll into balls.
instructions.6: Roll each ball on a cornflour-dusted surface, brushing between layers with oil.
instructions.7: Fry the ruqaq sheets on a ghee-greased tray over medium heat until golden on both sides.
instructions.8: In another pot, fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the black pepper, cinnamon, baharat and cardamom seeds.
instructions.9: Add the minced meat and stir until cooked and dry, then add the salt and sugar.
instructions.10: Make the ruqaq soak with the ghee, ishta and instant stock.
instructions.11: Lay a sheet of ruqaq in a ghee-greased tray, add 4–5 tablespoons of the soak, and repeat for all sheets.
instructions.12: Add the cooked mince and extras like nuts, raisins and cheese.
instructions.13: Cover the meat with another layer of ruqaq and repeat until everything is used.
instructions.14: Cut the ruqaq into squares or triangles before baking.
instructions.15: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 30 minutes until golden.

fah-284.title: Ruqaq with Cream (Meat Pie)
fah-284.culturalNotes: A small stock cube strengthens the broth. Grease the edges to stop the filling leaking.

instructions.1: Heat the ghee in a pan over the heat.
instructions.2: Add the minced onion and brown until golden.
instructions.3: Add the minced meat and stir with the onion until golden.
instructions.4: Add the cardamom, black pepper and salt and stir well.
instructions.5: Add the stock and milk and stir well.
instructions.6: Bring to the boil, then lower the heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Mix the ghee and baking powder in a small bowl.
instructions.8: Prepare the tray and grease with ghee.
instructions.9: Lay a sheet of ruqaq in the tray and smooth it well.
instructions.10: Add a layer of the meat-and-stock mixture.
instructions.11: Lay another ruqaq sheet and smooth it.
instructions.12: Add another layer of the meat-and-stock mixture.
instructions.13: Lay a final ruqaq sheet and smooth it.
instructions.14: Brush the surface with the ghee-and-baking-powder mix.

fah-285.title: Sausage & Cheese Filo Rolls
fah-285.culturalNotes: Add hot pepper if you like it spicy. Prepare the rolls ahead and refrigerate an hour before baking.

instructions.1: Prepare the filling: slice the onion and green pepper thinly.
instructions.2: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, add the onion and brown until golden.
instructions.3: Add the green pepper and stir for a minute.
instructions.4: Add the sausage cut into small pieces and stir for two minutes.
instructions.5: Add the salt, black pepper, seven-spice and tomato sauce and stir well.
instructions.6: Add the cumin and coriander and stir again.
instructions.7: Take the filling off the heat, cool slightly, then add the mozzarella and mix.
instructions.8: Make the rolls: brush the filo with a butter-and-oil or ghee-and-oil mix.
instructions.9: Put a portion of filling in the centre, roll tightly and seal the sides.
instructions.10: Arrange the rolls in a ghee-and-oil-greased tray.
instructions.11: Brush the tops with the rest of the fat mix.
instructions.12: Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 20 minutes until golden.
instructions.13: Take out and cover with foil for 5 minutes to keep them soft.

fah-286.title: Molto Sandwiches with Mixed Fillings
fah-286.culturalNotes: Use any filling you like — minced meat or shawarma. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky for tender, hollow sandwiches.

instructions.1: Mix the warm milk, warm water, salt, sugar, yeast and oil in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the flour gradually and mix until combined.
instructions.3: Knead for at least 10 minutes until soft and slightly tacky.
instructions.4: Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover with plastic and a towel, and prove in a switched-off oven.
instructions.5: Once proved, knock out the air and cut into small balls.
instructions.6: Fill each ball with your favourites (rumi cheese, barrel cheese, Nutella).
instructions.7: Roll each ball into a rectangle, put the filling in the centre and close into a roll.
instructions.8: Lay the sandwiches seam-side down on an oiled tray.
instructions.9: Prove once more.
instructions.10: Brush with beaten egg mixed with a little vinegar.
instructions.11: Bake in a hot oven for 10 minutes.
instructions.12: Cover the sandwiches with a damp towel straight out of the oven to keep them soft.

fah-287.title: Soft Cheese & Parsley Sandwiches
fah-287.culturalNotes: Change the filling as you like — minced meat or scrambled eggs work. The sandwiches keep in the fridge for two days.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the warm water gradually and knead until combined.
instructions.3: Add the oil and mix well until soft and not sticky.
instructions.4: Cover with a plastic bag and prove for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Prepare the filling of cheese, parsley and minced pepper.
instructions.6: Shape the dough into equal balls and roll them out.
instructions.7: Put the filling in the centre and seal the edges by hand and with a fork.
instructions.8: Dust a tray with a little flour and lay the sandwiches on it.
instructions.9: Heat a pan over medium heat with a spoon of oil.
instructions.10: Fry the sandwiches until golden on both sides.

fah-288.title: Soft Kaiser Sandwiches, Stuffed
fah-288.culturalNotes: Change the filling as you like — cheese and sausage or cheese and sugar. The sandwiches freeze well.

instructions.1: Mix half a cup of warm water with half a cup of warm milk, a tablespoon of sugar and a tablespoon of yeast. Cover and leave 10 minutes to activate.
instructions.2: Mix 3 cups of bread flour, 4 tablespoons of milk powder and a teaspoon of baking powder in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Add the yeast mix to the flour, then half a cup of oil and half a teaspoon of salt. Knead well.
instructions.4: If the dough needs it, add warm water a spoon at a time until smooth.
instructions.5: Cover with a plastic bag and clean towels and prove in a warm place for an hour.
instructions.6: Cut the dough into 18 lemon-sized balls.
instructions.7: Stuff each ball with pastrami and cheese and seal well.
instructions.8: Lay the sandwiches on an oiled tray or one lined with baking paper.
instructions.9: Cover and prove for 15 minutes.
instructions.10: Heat the oven to 180°C.
instructions.11: Bake the sandwiches for 20–25 minutes until golden.
instructions.12: Take out and cool slightly before serving.

fah-289.title: Shaboura (Dunking Cake)
fah-289.culturalNotes: Serve shaboura plain or dunked in milky or plain tea. Its baking smell fills the house, especially in winter.

instructions.1: Sift the flour and baking powder into a bowl.
instructions.2: Put the sugar, oil, ghee, vanilla and salt in the blender and blend until pale.
instructions.3: Add the flour-and-baking-powder mix to the liquids and mix well.
instructions.4: Add the hot milk gradually until the batter is uniform.
instructions.5: Grease a tray with ghee and sprinkle toasted sesame.
instructions.6: Pour the batter in and bake in a preheated 170°C oven for 45 minutes.
instructions.7: Take it out and test for doneness.
instructions.8: Serve hot, or cut in half and dunk in milky or plain tea.

fah-290.title: Quick Bread Slices
fah-290.culturalNotes: Serve for breakfast or supper — great lunchbox food for students. Fill with butter and cheese or anything you like.

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix a cup of warm milk with a tablespoon of sugar and a tablespoon of instant yeast. Leave for 10 minutes to prove.
instructions.2: In another bowl, mix 3½ cups of bread flour with half a teaspoon of salt and a teaspoon of baking powder.
instructions.3: Add the proved milk to the flour with a tablespoon of vinegar and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Knead until soft and cohesive.
instructions.4: Cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes until doubled.
instructions.5: Roll the dough on a floured surface to about a centimetre thick.
instructions.6: Cut into squares of a good size.
instructions.7: Heat a lightly oiled griddle, lay the slices on it, cover and prove for 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Make the glaze: mix a quarter cup of olive oil with a teaspoon of minced garlic, a teaspoon of fresh thyme and a teaspoon of smoked paprika.
instructions.9: Brush the slices with the glaze and bake at the highest heat for 10 minutes until golden.
instructions.10: Serve hot, filled with butter and cheese or anything you like.

fah-291.title: Cotton-Soft Flaky Dough
fah-291.culturalNotes: Use this dough for sweet or savoury pastries. The pastries freeze for a long time — shape and fill as you like.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the egg white, yogurt and oil and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the soda water a little at a time until the dough comes together.
instructions.4: Knead for 10 minutes until soft and smooth.
instructions.5: Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover and prove in a warm place for an hour.
instructions.6: Shape into small balls on a flour-dusted tray.
instructions.7: Roll each ball to half a centimetre and shape as you like.
instructions.8: Brush the tops with vinegar diluted with water and bake in a 220°C oven.
instructions.9: Bake for 10–15 minutes until golden.
instructions.10: Cool before freezing or serving.

fah-292.title: Flaky Dough for Bread & Bakes
fah-292.culturalNotes: Use this dough for pizza, manaqeesh and more. It keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix 3 cups of warm water with 2 tablespoons of yeast, a teaspoon of sugar, a teaspoon of salt and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Mix well and cover for 10 minutes until the yeast reacts and bubbles appear.
instructions.3: Add the kilo of flour gradually and mix until a soft dough forms.
instructions.4: Cover and leave for 30 minutes to prove and double.
instructions.5: After 30 minutes, wet your hands and fold the dough from all four sides; cover for another 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Repeat the fold-and-cover twice more, 30 minutes each.
instructions.7: After the third fold, wet your hands and fold once more; cover for 30 minutes.
instructions.8: Wet your hands, fold the dough one last time and cover for 30 minutes.
instructions.9: Dust the worktop with flour and semolina and roll the dough.
instructions.10: Cut into equal pieces and fill with thyme and olives or cheese, labneh, watercress and cherry tomatoes.
instructions.11: Lay the pieces on an oiled tray for 10 minutes.
instructions.12: Bake in a preheated 250°C oven for 10–15 minutes until golden.
instructions.13: Take out and cool slightly before serving.

fah-293.title: Japanese Fluffy Hollow Dough
fah-293.culturalNotes: Shape the dough and fill it any way you like. It turns out flaky and hollow — perfect for gatherings.

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix 6 cups of warm milk with 3 tablespoons of flour, stirring cold.
instructions.2: Put the mix over the heat and stir constantly until the flour cooks and it turns creamy.
instructions.3: Take it off the heat and cool slightly.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix the yeast with 3 tablespoons of sugar, a tablespoon of milk powder and 1½ teaspoons of salt.
instructions.5: Add the egg and milk and mix well.
instructions.6: Add the cooled cooked paste to the mix and knead well.
instructions.7: Add the 80 g of soft butter and knead until soft and not sticky.
instructions.8: Cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes.
instructions.9: Once proved, cut into small balls and shape like muffins or cup pizzas.
instructions.10: Add your favourite filling, sweet or savoury.
instructions.11: Put the balls in cupcake moulds and bake in a preheated 220°C oven for 10 minutes.
instructions.12: Serve hot or cold as you like.

fah-294.title: Spongy Pan Bread (No Oven)
fah-294.culturalNotes: Serve the flatbreads with white cheese, honey or any filling. The dough should be slightly tacky for a fluffy result.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and water.
instructions.2: Leave in a warm place for 10 minutes to activate.
instructions.3: Add the salt and egg and mix.
instructions.4: Add the flour gradually and knead with the warm water.
instructions.5: Add the oil and knead for 5 minutes until elastic and tacky.
instructions.6: Cover with plastic and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Cut the dough into 6 pieces and oil them.
instructions.8: Rest the pieces for 10 minutes.
instructions.9: Heat a pan over medium heat with two tablespoons of oil.
instructions.10: Take a piece of dough and stretch it on an oiled surface.
instructions.11: Cook the flatbread in the pan, covered, until coloured underneath, then flip.
instructions.12: Repeat with the rest of the dough.

fah-295.title: Paratha Bread
fah-295.culturalNotes: Serve paratha with honey, clotted cream, white cheese and chips, or with any dish you like.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the water gradually, kneading until cohesive and not sticky.
instructions.3: Knead well until smooth.
instructions.4: Cut the dough into equal balls (about 10–14).
instructions.5: Cover the balls with a plastic bag and rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Oil the pan and roll each ball thin.
instructions.7: Cook on the hot pan over medium heat.
instructions.8: Flip until golden on both sides.
instructions.9: Repeat until all the balls are done.

fah-296.title: Bakakeen Bread
fah-296.culturalNotes: Bake on a griddle if you have one. The bread turns soft and tasty in a hot oven.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast with the sugar and warm water and leave for 10 minutes to react.
instructions.2: Add the flour, butter-oil and vinegar and knead well.
instructions.3: Add the yeast and knead until soft and not sticky.
instructions.4: Add the laban rayeb or yogurt a little at a time until the dough balls up.
instructions.5: Add the salt after 5 minutes of kneading and knead again.
instructions.6: Prove until doubled.
instructions.7: Cut into small balls and rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.8: Roll each ball thin with flour.
instructions.9: Arrange the loaves on a baking tray, spaced apart.
instructions.10: Bake in a hot oven (top and bottom heat) until golden.
instructions.11: Cool slightly before serving.

fah-297.title: Cotton Bread
fah-297.culturalNotes: The bread keeps in a sealed bag for up to 3 days. Serve with cheese, hummus or any filling.

instructions.1: Heat the water very hot, pour it over the semolina flour and stir well.
instructions.2: Add the plain flour, sugar, yeast, salt, butter and cream cheese to the mixer and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the semolina paste to the rest and knead for at least 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Grease a deep dish with oil, put the dough in, oil the top and cover with plastic and a clean towel.
instructions.5: Prove until doubled.
instructions.6: Cut the dough into small balls (mandarin-sized).
instructions.7: Roll each ball and shape into a roll or circle.
instructions.8: Prove again until doubled.
instructions.9: Brush with a mix of milk powder, instant coffee and sugar.
instructions.10: Score the tops with a sharp blade.
instructions.11: Leave for 10 minutes.
instructions.12: Bake in a hot 220°C oven for 10 minutes on the lowest shelf.
instructions.13: Out of the oven, sprinkle with water and cover with a clean towel.

fah-298.title: Fluffy Turkish Bread
fah-298.culturalNotes: Serve with cheese and a cup of tea for a tasty breakfast. Homemade bread tastes and smells completely different from shop-bought.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, baking powder, yeast, salt and sugar in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the egg white, warm milk and warm water and knead for 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the oil and knead for 5 more minutes until soft and elastic.
instructions.4: Put in an oiled dish, cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove until doubled.
instructions.5: Shape into 4 equal balls on an oiled griddle, spaced apart.
instructions.6: Cover the balls and rest them.
instructions.7: Mix the egg yolk with a tablespoon of yogurt and brush over the loaves.
instructions.8: Add nigella seeds or sesame to taste.
instructions.9: Bake at the highest heat on the lowest shelf until cooked.
instructions.10: Leave in until golden.

fah-299.title: Arabic Bread
fah-299.culturalNotes: Make sure the dough proves well in a warm place. Bake in the oven or on a pan as you prefer.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking powder in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the milk powder, butter and yogurt and knead well.
instructions.3: Knead in a mixer for at least 10 minutes until smooth and not sticky.
instructions.4: Cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove in a warm place for an hour.
instructions.5: Cut the dough into egg-sized balls.
instructions.6: Cover the balls for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Roll each ball to 3–4 mm thick.
instructions.8: Arrange the loaves on an oiled tray.
instructions.9: Or griddle each loaf 30 seconds per side over medium heat.
instructions.10: On a pan, bake 30 seconds per side too.
instructions.11: Bake the loaves in the oven for 10 minutes until golden.

fah-300.title: Yeast-Free Country Bread
fah-300.culturalNotes: Keep the dough cohesive and thin when rolling. The bread keeps in a sealed bag for a few days.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt, sugar and baking powder in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the oil and yogurt and knead with warm water until combined.
instructions.3: Knead well until cohesive and smooth.
instructions.4: Divide into equal small balls.
instructions.5: Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Roll each ball on a floured surface until very thin.
instructions.7: Heat a pan over high heat and lay the thin bread on it.
instructions.8: Cook until it spots and changes colour slightly, then flip.
instructions.9: Cover after cooking to keep it soft and hot.

fah-301.title: Potato Fino Rolls
fah-301.culturalNotes: Use the fino rolls for breakfast or lunch sandwiches. They keep in a sealed bag for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the mashed potatoes, warm milk and egg white. Knead well.
instructions.3: If the dough needs it, add warm water a spoon at a time until it comes together.
instructions.4: Knead for 5 minutes, add the oil, then knead 5 more minutes.
instructions.5: Cover and prove until doubled.
instructions.6: Take small balls of dough and arrange on an oiled griddle.
instructions.7: Prove once more.
instructions.8: Brush with egg yolk mixed with a spoon of milk, then sprinkle sesame.
instructions.9: Bake at the highest heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.10: Cover for 5 minutes after baking to stop them drying.

fah-302.title: Shepherd's Pie
fah-302.culturalNotes: Serve hot with a green salad or a side of your choice. The pie keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days.

instructions.1: Peel and dice the potatoes, then boil until soft.
instructions.2: Put the boiled potatoes in a bowl with the spice, salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons of butter. Mash well.
instructions.3: Add a cup of milk and stir until combined.
instructions.4: Add the cheese, stir, then chill the mixture.
instructions.5: In another pot, put the meat cut into small pieces with the peas.
instructions.6: Add a tablespoon of flour and stir.
instructions.7: Add the stock cube and stir again.
instructions.8: Cook over the heat until the flour toasts and combines with the meat and peas.
instructions.9: In a baking tray, lay the potato mix first, then the meat-and-pea mix on top.
instructions.10: Sprinkle paprika on top to taste.
instructions.11: Bake in a preheated 180°C oven for 20 minutes until golden.

fah-303.title: Pot-Braised Kebab Pie
fah-303.culturalNotes: Serve the pie with the leftover pot sauce. It keeps in the fridge for two days or longer frozen.

instructions.1: Make the filling: cube the meat, wedge the onions, cube and brown the potatoes.
instructions.2: Heat the ghee and oil in a pot, add the meat with mastic and bay leaf and brown it.
instructions.3: Add the onions and stir well, then add the sugar and stir.
instructions.4: Cover the pot, lower the heat and leave until the meat cooks.
instructions.5: Add two cups of water, boil, then cover and finish cooking.
instructions.6: Make the dough: mix the flour with the yeast, sugar, baking powder and salt, then add the laban and warm water and knead.
instructions.7: Rest the dough for 10 minutes, then divide into an even number of pieces.
instructions.8: Roll the dough half a centimetre thick and lay one layer in an oiled tray.
instructions.9: Add the filling on the bottom layer and cover with the second layer of dough.
instructions.10: Brush the top with a milk-powder, Nescafé and sugar mix, then sprinkle sesame or nigella seeds.
instructions.11: Bake at 200°C for 10 minutes, then grill until the top browns.
instructions.12: Repeat for the second pie.

fah-304.title: Meat & Potato Pinwheel Pastries
fah-304.culturalNotes: The pastries keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen in bags.

instructions.1: Make the filling: grate the potatoes and onions and drain well.
instructions.2: Mix the minced meat with the potato, onion, salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, chilli, seven-spice and sugar. Mix well.
instructions.3: Make the dough: mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in a bowl. Add water gradually and knead until smooth and elastic.
instructions.4: Add 2–3 tablespoons of oil and knead again. Cover and rest for 30–60 minutes.
instructions.5: Roll the dough into a square about half a centimetre thick.
instructions.6: Spread the filling over the dough and roll into a log.
instructions.7: Cut the log into pieces 2–3 cm wide.
instructions.8: Heat a pan over medium heat with a little oil. Fry the pieces until golden on both sides.
instructions.9: Serve hot with pickles, hummus sauce and parsley.

fah-305.title: Qaraqesh Bites
fah-305.culturalNotes: Swap the oil for ghee or a mix of both. Qaraqesh keeps in an airtight tin for a long time.

instructions.1: Put the flour in a deep dish.
instructions.2: Add the sugar, toasted sesame, salt, baking powder, yeast and fennel or anise. Mix well.
instructions.3: Add the oil and rub until the flour absorbs it.
instructions.4: Add the water gradually and knead until cohesive.
instructions.5: Cover and rest in a warm place for 15 minutes.
instructions.6: Roll the dough into a rectangle on baking paper.
instructions.7: Cut into small pieces.
instructions.8: Lay the pieces on a tray lined with baking paper.
instructions.9: Bake in a preheated 170°C oven for 10 minutes.
instructions.10: Serve with cream cheese, olive oil and mint.

fah-306.title: Whole-Grain Soft Discs
fah-306.culturalNotes: Serve the discs with honey and jam or savoury cheese with a cup of mint tea. They keep in a sealed bag for two days.

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix the cup of warm water with the spoon of sugar.
instructions.2: Add the spoon of instant yeast and mix. Cover and leave for 10 minutes to puff.
instructions.3: In a pan, heat half a cup of oil with half a cup of ghee. When hot, take off the heat and add two spoons of cream and two of sugar. Mix well.
instructions.4: Add the hot mix to the yeast mix and stir well.
instructions.5: Add half a teaspoon of salt and mix well.
instructions.6: Add the kilo of whole-grain flour gradually until the dough comes together — add another cup of water if dry.
instructions.7: Knead until soft and lump-free. Don't over-knead or it toughens.
instructions.8: Cover and prove for 30 minutes until doubled.
instructions.9: Cut into equal balls and space them on an oiled tray.
instructions.10: Flatten each ball — thin but not too thin — and prove again for 30 minutes.
instructions.11: Heat the oven to high. Bake the discs on the floor level until golden underneath, then grill to colour the tops.
instructions.12: Serve hot with labneh, olives, tahini and mint tea.

fah-307.title: Soft Cream Discs
fah-307.culturalNotes: Serve the soft cream discs with tea or coffee. They keep in a sealed bag for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Warm the milk, add the sugar, cream and yeast, mix well and set aside.
instructions.2: In another bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt.
instructions.3: Add the yogurt, ghee and vinegar to the flour and mix until combined.
instructions.4: Add the milk-and-cream mix to the flour and mix until a dough forms.
instructions.5: Knead for 4 minutes until soft and smooth.
instructions.6: Cover with a clean towel and put in a warm switched-off oven for 10 minutes to speed proving.
instructions.7: Once proved, cut into small pieces and roll into balls.
instructions.8: Oil a griddle and space the balls on it.
instructions.9: Prove for 10 minutes.
instructions.10: Flatten the balls slightly and bake on the lowest shelf of a preheated oven for 10 minutes until golden.
instructions.11: Cool slightly before serving.

fah-308.title: Soft Country Discs
fah-308.culturalNotes: Keep the dough very soft and prove the discs twice for the best result. The oven must be very hot before baking. Cover them after baking to keep them soft.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, milk powder, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Activate the yeast with the sugar and leave until it rises.
instructions.3: Melt the butter, oil and cream over low heat.
instructions.4: Add the butter-oil-cream mix to the flour while stirring.
instructions.5: Add the yogurt and the yeast mix and knead until soft.
instructions.6: Cover and prove until doubled.
instructions.7: Cut into small balls and prove again.
instructions.8: Stuff the balls with date paste, cinnamon-sugar or cheese and halva.
instructions.9: Flatten each ball, close over the filling and seal well.
instructions.10: Arrange the discs on the baking griddle and prove once more.
instructions.11: Heat the oven to 220°C.
instructions.12: Bake the discs until done.
instructions.13: Cover them straight out of the oven to stay soft.
instructions.14: Store in freezer bags once fully cool.

fah-309.title: Country Discs
fah-309.culturalNotes: Serve the country discs hot with tea or coffee. They keep in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast and sugar in a cup of warm water and set aside for 10 minutes to activate.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, salt, baking powder and milk powder in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Add the yogurt, cream, oil and butter to the flour and mix well.
instructions.4: Add the warm water gradually until a soft, smooth dough forms.
instructions.5: Cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Cut into lemon-sized balls.
instructions.7: Roll each ball on a floured surface to about half a centimetre.
instructions.8: Bake the discs on an oiled tray in a 200°C oven for 10–15 minutes until golden.
instructions.9: For the filling, soften the date paste with a teaspoon of butter and sesame, put it in the centre of a disc and seal.
instructions.10: Bake the stuffed discs the same way.

fah-310.title: Pizza Bombs
fah-310.culturalNotes: Add or remove filling ingredients to taste. Serve the bombs hot with tomato sauce or ketchup.

instructions.1: Mix the yeast and sugar in a cup of warm water and leave for 10 minutes to activate.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, salt and baking powder in a bowl.
instructions.3: Add the yeast mix gradually with the warm milk and knead until combined.
instructions.4: Add the ghee and oil and mix well.
instructions.5: Knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
instructions.6: Put in an oiled dish, cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove for an hour.
instructions.7: Cut the dough into 12 pieces and roll into balls.
instructions.8: Cover the balls again for 10 minutes.
instructions.9: Make the filling by mixing the cheese, tomatoes, peppers, olives, thyme and ketchup.
instructions.10: Roll each ball and put a tablespoon of filling in the centre.
instructions.11: Wrap the filling in the dough and roll into a ball.
instructions.12: Dip the balls in milk, then in breadcrumbs.
instructions.13: Arrange on an oiled dish and prove for 30 minutes.
instructions.14: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the balls until golden all over.

fah-311.title: Secret-Filling Filo Pastries
fah-311.culturalNotes: Add fresh thyme to the filling if you like. Great with tea.

instructions.1: Mix the butter, milk, yogurt, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl until combined.
instructions.2: Take a filo sheet and brush with the secret mix.
instructions.3: Lay another sheet on top and brush it too.
instructions.4: Cut the sheets in half, then lengthwise.
instructions.5: Brush the top with the secret mix again.
instructions.6: Put the filling on the sheet and close the edges.
instructions.7: Beat the egg with the vinegar.
instructions.8: Brush the tops until nicely browned and shiny.
instructions.9: Put the pastries on a baking tray into the middle shelf of the oven.
instructions.10: Bake until golden.

fah-312.title: Brioche Roses
fah-312.culturalNotes: The dough should be soft and elastic when kneaded and proved in a warm place. The roses keep in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: In a pan, mix the flour, sugar, milk powder, yeast and salt.
instructions.2: Add the warm milk, butter and egg and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the vinegar and vanilla and mix again.
instructions.4: Knead in the mixer for at least 10 minutes until soft and elastic.
instructions.5: Put in an oiled bowl, cover with plastic and a clean towel and prove in a warm place until doubled.
instructions.6: Once proved, cut into small balls and cover.
instructions.7: Roll each ball into an oval and brush with butter.
instructions.8: Roll it over itself and cut into small pieces.
instructions.9: Wrap the pieces around each other to form roses.
instructions.10: Put the roses on an oiled tray, spaced apart.
instructions.11: Prove the roses again.
instructions.12: Make the glaze from the egg, milk and Nescafé and brush the roses.
instructions.13: Lightly sprinkle sugar on the roses.
instructions.14: Bake in a hot 220°C oven on the lowest shelf until golden.
instructions.15: Turn off the bottom heat and run the top until the roses colour.
instructions.16: Out of the oven, sprinkle sugar dissolved in water and cover with a towel for 5 minutes before serving.

fah-313.title: Sausage Roses
fah-313.culturalNotes: The dough also makes pizza and doughnuts. It keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Mix the sugar and yeast in the warm water and stir well.
instructions.2: Leave for 10 minutes to confirm the yeast is active.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, mix the flour, milk powder, baking powder and salt.
instructions.4: Add the yogurt and mayonnaise to the dry ingredients and knead well.
instructions.5: Knead for 10 minutes until soft and cohesive.
instructions.6: Cover and prove in a warm place for an hour until doubled.
instructions.7: Cut into equal balls.
instructions.8: Roll each ball into a thin rectangle.
instructions.9: Lay a sausage on the dough and roll it up.
instructions.10: Seal the ends well and make 3–4 slits across the sausage.
instructions.11: Put the roses on an oiled tray and prove for 15 minutes.
instructions.12: In a small bowl, mix the egg yolk, milk and instant coffee.
instructions.13: Brush the roses and sprinkle nigella seeds or sesame to taste.
instructions.15: Bake the tray for 20 minutes until golden.
